title: Rhythmic windowed token regulator and kernel-aware prefetch orchestration
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Problem: Production traces show persistent 95th/99th token-latency spikes during mixed short/long request traffic even after kernel affinity and basic batching heuristics. These spikes correlate with bursts where many short requests collide with long prefill operations and where kernel selection oscillates between dense and sparse attention kernels, causing transient kernel warmup and NVLink congestion. Existing admission policies are coarse (per-slot or global token buckets) and do not account for temporal rhythm of incoming requests or kernel transition costs.

Goal: Implement a rhythmic windowed token regulator that: (1) observes short-timescale traffic rhythms and builds prognostic micro-windows to gate prefetch/admission decisions, (2) fuses kernel selection signals (profiler hints + attention sparsity estimates) so admission favors grouping requests with compatible kernel paths, and (3) adds a lightweight probabilistic prefetch backoff to reduce kernel warmup churn while retaining throughput. Target: reduce 95th token latency by 20% and 99th by 30% on our mixed workload benchmarks without harming 50th latency or throughput >95% baseline.

Design overview:
- Rhythm detection: sliding micro-window (25-200ms) that maintains decayed counts of short-prefill vs long-prefill requests per GPU. Use exponential smoothing to estimate the next-window composition (prognostic score).
- Windowed gating: convert prognostic score into admission quotas per micro-window. Quotas are soft and shaped by tenant priority and per-tenant kernel-affinity score.
- Kernel signal fusion: runtime profiler exposes a compact kernel affinity tag per inflight request (eg "dense-attn-v2", "sparse-attn-hybrid"). The regulator attempts to admit batches where >70% requests share affinity; otherwise it applies a short, randomized hold (2-8 ms) to wait for compatible requests or fall back to a compatible kernel variant.
- Probabilistic prefetch backoff: for detected oscillations where kernel-selection flips more than N times within T seconds, apply an exponential backoff on new prefetch-triggering admissions for that GPU. Backoff decays on stable windows.
- KV-cache hinting: when gating delays prefill admit, inject a lightweight cache-prefetch hint path to warm attention KV regions for long requests scheduled later in the same window to avoid full kernel warmup cost. This uses existing KV cache prefetch APIs with capped bandwidth.

Integration with existing systems:
- Admission controller: plug into admission pipeline as a pre-admit filter. It emits quota decisions and hints to the batch shaper.
- Kernel profiler: uses the kernel hint API from the profiler service (runtime-metrics). If affinity tag missing, falls back to static model-profile heuristics.
- Metrics: add new metrics: micro_window_composition, admitted_batch_affinity_ratio, kernel_switch_count, prefetch_backoff_active, kv_prefetch_bytes. Add per-tenant and per-gpu dimensions.

Rollout plan:
1) Canary on staging with synthetic mixed workloads (short: 8-30 tokens, long: 512-1024).
2) Small production canary (5% of traffic) on dedicated pool; collect latency quantiles and kernel_switch_count.
3) Ramp to 25% if 95th/99th improve and throughput loss <5%.
4) Full rollout with kill-switch gated by console metric alerts.

Testing & experiments:
- A/B harness in perf cluster with multi-tenant mixes; baseline is current admission + kernel-affinity disabled.
- Experiment 1: vary micro-window sizes [25, 50, 100, 200ms] and smoothing half-life to find sweet spot for different traffic shapes.
- Experiment 2: affinity threshold tuning (60/70/80%) and randomized hold distribution (2/4/8 ms).

Success metrics:
- 95th token latency decrease >= 20% on mixed workload benchmark.
- 99th token latency decrease >= 30% on mixed workload benchmark.
- Throughput preserved at >= 95% of baseline.
- Kernel switch count reduction >= 40%.

Implementation tasks (high level):
- regulator core: micro-window detector + quota calculator (runtime)
- kernel-signal adaptor: consume profiler tags and annotate requests (runtime/ingest)
- batch shaper hook: accept gate decisions and apply randomized holds (batching service)
- KV-prefetch integration: lightweight hint path implementation (kvcache service)
- metrics & dashboards: add charts to console and create alert rules

Risks & mitigations:
- Overly aggressive holds could increase P50 latency for latency-sensitive tenants. Mitigate by per-tenant SLO caps and immediate bypass for high-priority tokens.
- Incorrect affinity tagging could delay batches unnecessarily; fallback to time-based quotas after N misses.
- Prefetch bandwidth could increase cost; cap prefetch bytes and add accounting to billing metrics.

Open design decisions:
- default micro-window size and smoothing parameters (tuning required in experiments).
- affinity threshold for grouping vs fallback.

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Rhythmic+Windowed+Token+Regulator
- Perf harness (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-perf/tree/feature/rhythmic-regulator
- Initial prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4721
- Staging dashboard (Influx): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/uid/rhythmic-regulator

Next steps: finish kernel-signal adaptor, wire batch shaper hook, run first micro-window sweep experiment in perf cluster, and create canary configuration (5% traffic) in orchestra config.
